scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Users on pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) and pc_0_1 (10.0.1.2) report they cannot
reach each other in either direction. Both hosts can still ping their
own gateways (10.0.0.1 and 10.0.1.1). The NOC insists the fabric is
healthy: every BGP session is Established, all routes are present on
every router, no interface has flapped, and all FRR daemons are
running. Identify what is silently eating the traffic.

injection.action: add a FORWARD DROP rule for pc_0_0 -> pc_0_1 transit

post_inject_check.expect: 0% loss   (gateway still OK -- INPUT chain untouched)

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: leaf_router_0_0 iptables FORWARD chain
Mechanism: a DROP rule on leaf_router_0_0 discards every forwarded
  packet with source in 10.0.0.0/24 and destination in 10.0.1.0/24.
  All pc_0_0 traffic must transit leaf_router_0_0 (its only gateway),
  so pc_0_0 -> pc_0_1 packets die there. The reverse direction fails
  too, despite matching no rule on its way in: pc_0_1's echo requests
  ARE delivered to pc_0_0, but pc_0_0's replies (src 10.0.0.2, dst
  10.0.1.2) match the rule and are dropped -- a one-directional filter
  breaks bidirectional traffic. Routing and BGP are completely
  healthy; the drop is at the firewall layer. Local delivery to the
  gateway itself uses the INPUT chain, which is untouched, so both
  hosts still ping their gateways.
Localization: leaf_router_0_0
Root cause: extraneous iptables FORWARD DROP rule
  (-s 10.0.0.0/24 -d 10.0.1.0/24) on leaf_router_0_0
Fix: `iptables -D FORWARD -s 10.0.0.0/24 -d 10.0.1.0/24 -j DROP` on
  leaf_router_0_0
scenario.fix_spec:
remove the DROP rule on leaf_router_0_0 --
`iptables -D FORWARD -s 10.0.0.0/24 -d 10.0.1.0/24 -j DROP`
scoring_axes: must-identify-component: iptables FORWARD DROP / firewall filter
must-recognize-filter-pattern: recognizes healthy routing + healthy BGP with silent forwarding loss as a packet-filter fault, not a routing fault
bonus-explains-asymmetric-drop: explains that the single directional rule (10.0.0.0/24 -> 10.0.1.0/24) also kills the reverse ping because replies match it

agent.diagnosis_text:
The fabric control plane (BGP/FRR) and interfaces look healthy, but the data plane on leaf_router_0_0 is being filtered by the host firewall. On leaf_router_0_0 the Linux netfilter/iptables FORWARD chain contains an explicit drop for inter-subnet traffic: “-A FORWARD -s 10.0.0.0/24 -d 10.0.1.0/24 -j DROP”. The nftables ruleset mirrors this with a forward chain rule “ip saddr 10.0.0.0/24 ip daddr 10.0.1.0/24 … drop”, and its counters show packets being dropped (counter packets 29 bytes 2172), proving it is actively eating these flows.

Mechanism: Traffic from pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) to pc_0_1 (10.0.1.2) is dropped as soon as it hits leaf_router_0_0 for forwarding towards the spines, so pings/traceroute from 10.0.0.0/24 die after the first hop. In the reverse direction, requests from pc_0_1 can reach 10.0.0.2 via the fabric, but the echo-replies sourced from 10.0.0.2 back to 10.0.1.2 are also forwarded by leaf_router_0_0 and match the same DROP rule, so no replies are seen. This matches traceroute behavior and explains why each host can still ping its own gateway (locally terminated traffic is unaffected).

Localization: leaf_router_0_0 kernel netfilter, FORWARD chain (policy override), not an FRR/BGP issue.

Root cause: A stray iptables/nftables ACL on leaf_router_0_0 dropping 10.0.0.0/24 → 10.0.1.0/24 traffic.

Corrective fix: Remove/disable the rule (e.g., iptables -D FORWARD -s 10.0.0.0/24 -d 10.0.1.0/24 -j DROP and delete the equivalent nft rule), then persist the clean policy and verify end-to-end pings.

per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly names leaf_router_0_0 as the location (kernel netfilter/iptables FORWARD chain) of the DROP rule multiple times.

per_axis.axis: must-identify-component: iptables FORWARD DROP / firewall filter
per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly identifies the kernel netfilter/iptables FORWARD chain DROP rule (and nftables equivalent) on leaf_router_0_0 as the filtering component causing the failure.

per_axis.axis: must-recognize-filter-pattern: recognizes healthy routing + healthy BGP with silent forwarding loss as a packet-filter fault, not a routing fault
per_axis.rationale: The writeup explicitly states BGP/FRR and interfaces are healthy and correctly attributes the silent forwarding loss to an iptables/nftables FORWARD DROP rule on leaf_router_0_0.

per_axis.axis: bonus-explains-asymmetric-drop: explains that the single directional rule (10.0.0.0/24 -> 10.0.1.0/24) also kills the reverse ping because replies match it
per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly states that pc_0_1's requests reach pc_0_0 but the echo-replies (src 10.0.0.2 → dst 10.0.1.2) are forwarded by leaf_router_0_0 and match the same DROP rule, explaining the asymmetric failure.
The agent explicitly recommends deleting the iptables DROP and the equivalent nft rule and persisting the policy, which matches the expected fix.

The investigation log explicitly shows the FORWARD DROP rule on leaf_router_0_0 and includes supporting connectivity tests (failed inter-host pings/traceroutes, successful gateway pings, rp_filter disabled, tc showing no drops) that together justify the firewall-as-cause explanation. Some nft counter details cited in the writeup are truncated in the log, but the core evidence and logic are present and consistent.
